article.description: DeLisha Milton had 13 of her 17 points in the first seven minutes after halftime as the Sparks beat the Utah Starzz 75-67 Thursday night in the opening game of the Western Conference finals.
article.headline: Sparks make life for Starzz unpleasant early
article.linkText: Milton leads Sparks' opening win in Utah
article.story:
SALT LAKE CITY (AP) -- DeLisha Milton couldn't stop shooting. It
seemed she couldn't miss, either.

	   Milton scored 13 of her 17 points in the first seven minutes
after halftime as the Los Angeles Sparks beat the Utah Starzz 75-67
Thursday night in Game 1 of the Western Conference finals.

	   "My teammates did a great job of finding the open person and it
was me,'' Milton said.

	   Leading 34-32 at halftime, the Sparks planned to attack 7-foot-2
Margo Dydek because the Utah center had picked up four first-half
fouls.

	   But Dydek stayed back on defense, and Milton made the Starzz
pay. She hit a layup and connected twice on 3-pointers in the first
three minutes.

	   "I just happened to be behind the 3-point line a few times and
Margo wouldn't come out of the paint,'' Milton said. "I took the
shots that were given to me, and they were falling.''

	   Utah gets another chance in Game 2 of the best-of-three series
on Saturday in Los Angeles, but trends don't favor an upset. The
Sparks, last year's WNBA champions, swept the three-game season
series and improved to 16-6 overall against Utah.

	   Tamecka Dixon scored 13 for the Sparks, who also got 11 each
from Mwadi Mabika and Nikki Teasley. Lisa Leslie had 12 points but
was held scoreless in the second half, though she finished with
seven blocked shots.

	   "I just tried to stay focused and play defense,'' Leslie said.
"Seven blocks, I'm very happy with that.''

	   Natalie Williams had 14 points and 11 rebounds, and Dydek scored
13 points for the Starzz, but it wasn't enough to offset Milton's
big night.

	   "The bottom line is that whoever Margo guards, whether it's
DeLisha or Lisa, she is going to have to get out and defend the
3-point shot,'' Utah coach Candi Harvey said. "They present
tremendous matchup problems at that position.''

	   Marie Ferdinand scored 13 points for the Starzz, who trailed by
as many as 15 points in the second half but made a late run,
getting to 65-55 on Jennifer Azzi's jumper with 5:08 to play.

	   The Sparks held on, using their deeper bench to wear down Utah.

	   "If you look at the Houston series, most of Utah's scoring came
from five players,'' Dixon said. "We have great players coming off
our bench, scorers who could probably start on other teams.''

	   The Starzz nabbed a homecourt victory to open the first-round
series against Houston, but their chances of another were dimmed by
14 first-half turnovers, only two fewer than Utah's season average
for a game.

	   The Starzz finished with 21 turnovers and shot 37 percent.

	   "We killed ourselves,'' Ferdinand said. "It wasn't anything
they did to us. We just need to take better care of the ball.''

	   Milton went 0-for-5 from the field in the first half but her
scoring surge after the break steadily put the Sparks ahead, and
Los Angeles improved to 11-1 in the postseason when it leads at
halftime.

	   "I didn't think about what happened in the first half,'' Milton
said. "I just waited to get my legs back.''

	   It was 53-42 when Milton hit a 3-pointer with 13:23 to play, and
she later contributed with a huge blocked shot against Williams.

	   Moments later, Milton rushed in to flatten Williams on a rebound
and then dumped a quick pass to a wide-open Latasha Byears for a
layup that gave Los Angeles a 69-56 lead with 2:38 to play,
spoiling Utah's first trip to the conference finals.
